news.title: Donnarumma calls on Italy supporters after ‘heartbreaking’ summer with no World Cup
news.lede: Gianluigi Donnarumma has rallied the Italy supporters, calling on them to help the Azzurri into a new era under Roberto Mancini after a ‘heartbreaking’ summer that left the squad watching the 2026 World Cup from home: ‘Together, we have to rewrite our history’. The Manchester City stopper and Italy national team captain spoke in-depth to Sky Sport Italia ahead of the upcoming September-October international break, which will see the Azzurri take on Belgium, Turkiye, France and Turkiye again in the Nations League. Donnarumma captained the side that lost to Bosnia and Herzegovina in the 2026 World Cup play-off final at the end of March, which led to a complete overhaul of the Italy national team set-up. Head coach Gennaro Gattuso has been replaced by Euro 2020 winner Mancini, Gianluigi Buffon has also left the delegation, as has FIGC President Gabriele Gravina.

news.title: How James Rodríguez turned World Cup fame into an $80 million fortune through football, endorsements and
news.lede: James Rodríguez closed the final chapter of his international career this week, retiring from Colombian duty with 131 caps after a 15-year run that began when he was barely old enough to drive. His farewell came days after the 2026 World Cup, where Colombia topped their group ahead of Portugal before falling to Switzerland on penalties in the round of 16. The retirement was not just the end of an era for Los Cafeteros. news.title: FULL LIST: From Messi to Fofana: Footballers who announced international retirement
news.lede: The 2026 FIFA World Cup marked the end of international careers for several established football stars, with a number of veterans announcing their retirement from international football following the tournament. From World Cup winners to long-serving national team captains, the list includes players from Europe, Africa and South America. PUNCH Online takes a look at 10 notable players who have ended their international careers or announced their departure from international football following the 2026 World Cup. Argentina captain Lionel Messi announced his retirement from international football after the 2026 World Cup, where his side reached the final.

news.title: Here we come! Young Ferns qualify for 2027 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: New Zealand have qualified for next year’s FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco after beating Papua New Guinea 3-0 in Honiara. The win, in the semi-finals of the OFC U-16 Women’s Championship, ensures New Zealand will be one of Oceania’s two representatives at the 2027 global tournament. It will be New Zealand’s 11th consecutive appearance at the U-16 World Cup. The second qualifying spot at the World Cup will go to either New Caledonia or Fiji, due to meet in Wednesday’s second semi-final.

news.title: Lionel Messi to bid farewell to Argentina national team with a final match in Buenos Aires: ‘The last tango of the world’s best player’
news.lede: A story that had it all, from painful defeats to everlasting victories, will come to an end. It will happen on October 6, when Lionel Messi plays his final match with the Argentina national team. That day the Albiceleste will face Benin in Buenos Aires in a friendly. “The last tango of the world’s best player,” said the president of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), Claudio Tapia.

news.title: Thomas Tuchel makes bizarre admission about eating World Cup grass
news.lede: Thomas Tuchel looks back on Mexico City celebrations with some regret (Picture: PA Wire) England manager Thomas Tuchel has a strange regret about the World Cup over the summer, wishing he had eaten some Mexican grass when he got the chance. The Three Lions had an eventful journey at the World Cup, reaching the semi-finals where they suffered a dramatic late defeat to Argentina. There were plenty of highs along the way, including the opening win over Croatia and finishing their tournament with a thrilling third-place play-off victory over France. The highlight for many, though, was the trip to the Azteca Stadium in the round of 16 and the tense 3-2 win England managed to secure over Mexico.
